_source.citation: Amate A, Lieberman M. Chiral sensitivity of medetomidine lateral flow immunoassay test strips. Harm Reduct J (2025). https://doi.org/10.1186/s12954-025-01387-6 (open access, CC BY 4.0; published online 2 January 2026)
_source.transcribed_from: Table 1 (lots), Table 2 (interference at 2 mg/mL), Table 3 and text (detomidine), Figure 4 and text (enantiomer response) of the article-in-press PDF
_source.protocol: Strips dipped 15 s in the test solution, read after 5 min against a 1-10 visual intensity scorecard (lateralDX #12082021); all solutions in 18 MOhm water (comparable to DI); interference: about 20 mg of each substance in 10 mL water (2 mg/mL), one strip per lot per substance. Per the manufacturers' directions any visible test line, however faint, counts as a negative result.
_source.scoring: 'Neg-N' = negative with a test line of intensity N on the scorecard; Neg-1 to Neg-3 is a faint line that might be misread as a false positive; 'Pos' = positive (no test line, intensity 0).
_source.not_included: Limit-of-detection curves (Figures 2 and 3), tap water and temperature results, and the dex:levo mixture grid values beyond the per-lot class below are plotted but not tabulated in the article; the supplementary information (SI Tables S2 and 4) was not part of this file.
caveats: Methods text lists WiseBatch lot 'MTM24100902'; Table 1, Table 2 and the figures all say MTM24120002. MTM24120002 is used here.

Detomidine (a different molecule from medetomidine) read positive on all seven lots at 2 mg/mL, and on the three BTNX lots tested (DOAB24080502, DOAB24100900, DOAB24100902) all strips were still positive at 0.07 mg/mL, with interference ceasing at 0.02 mg/mL (SI Table S2). The authors suggest this cross-reactivity 'may be a feature, not a bug'. It is an observed result, not a design property, and is treated here as an ordinary interferent.
Levamisole gave faint test lines (Neg-2 to Neg-4) on all lots at 2 mg/mL; the article notes these can be misread as false positives.
_source.submitter_rule: Each published lot carries the article citation as its 'submitter' (decided 2026-11-13); results can be merged with 2026 form data for the same lot later.
_source.target_note: The 2026 dashboard tests racemic medetomidine HCl; the article also tested pure dexmedetomidine and levomedetomidine (see chiral_response).

chiral_response_key.requires_both_enantiomers: Reads positive only when both dexmedetomidine and levomedetomidine are present; negative with 5000 ng/mL of either pure enantiomer, although the racemic LOD was below 2000 ng/mL (early BTNX lots).
chiral_response_key.dexmedetomidine_selective: Antibody selective for dexmedetomidine: positive whenever dexmedetomidine is above its LOD; racemic medetomidine is detected at about double that LOD (only the dex half acts). Labeled 'dexmedetomidine' strips (redesigned BTNX lots).
chiral_response_key.responds_to_dexmedetomidine_negative_to_: WiseBatch strips: positive for pure dexmedetomidine and for mixtures containing enough dexmedetomidine, negative for pure levomedetomidine. Per Figure 4, MTM25050002 stays positive down to 1000 ng/mL dex (with 5000 ng/mL levo) and MTM24120002 down to 3000 ng/mL dex.

enantiomer_grid_figure4.note: Read from the dot grid in Figure 4 (filled = positive). Columns are dexmedetomidine:levomedetomidine in ug/mL; every other mixture in the grid read negative. Transcribed by eye from a figure, so check against the SI before quoting.
